title: FICTIONAL — More consistent service routing
customer_brief: Fictional service owner deciding how to make intake and handover more consistent.

sections.challenge: A fictional service team used inconsistent intake categories, so ownership was unclear.
sections.contribution: The fictional consultant implemented intake normalization; the service owner defined policy and accepted handover.
sections.approach: Explicit categories and routing rules were piloted instead of an autonomous decision agent. Exceptions were documented for the service owner.
sections.outcome: The fictional service owner accepted the documented routing and exception process. No measured time or financial benefit is claimed.
sections.evidence: The synthetic pilot handover record v1 is the only attached source. It must be reviewed, not treated as real client evidence.
sections.limitations: Fictional pilot only. No production rollout, causal benefit, numerical saving or external permission is established.
sections.customer_fit: Useful as a design discussion when a service team has inconsistent intake and a named process owner.
sections.poor_fit: Not evidence for autonomous routing of regulated high-risk decisions or for teams without process ownership.

sources.excerpt: FICTIONAL TEST DATA, NOT A CLIENT RECORD. The service team had inconsistent intake categories. The consultant implemented normalization; the service owner owned routing policy and accepted the documented exceptions and handover. This was a pilot, with no measured savings or production rollout. It is useful only as a design discussion for comparable teams with process ownership. No permission for external customer reuse is recorded.
